newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-GOOSEN THREE AHEAD BEFORE PARIS WASHOUT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GOOSEN THREE AHEAD BEFORE PARIS WASHOUT.

text.p: A spectacular start by South African Retief Goosen helped him into a three-stroke lead before heavy rain caused play to be abandoned in the French Open at the National Golf Club on Thursday.

No players had finished their rounds when officials took the decision. Tournament favourite Colin Montgomerie of Scotland and defending champion Robert Allenby of Australia were two of the scheduled afternoon starters who could not play a shot.
Play resumes on Friday when it is hoped the first round can be completed.
The start was delayed three hours because the course was waterlogged after a night's rain.
After they did begin, incessant rain caused a suspension of play just before 1200 GMT.
The tournament director tried to restart at 1530 but another downpour brought the abandonment as players waited on the course to restart.

Not long after play began Goosen, 28, holed out with his second shot on the par-four 10th, his first hole. He hit a wedge shot 126 yards and watched it screw back into the cup from two feet behind the hole.
When he followed up with four birdies he was three ahead of Ireland's Paul McGinley and two English professionals, Roger Chapman and Martin Gates, with Scot Sandy Lyle a further stroke back.
Just after the stoppage a loud clap of thunder accompanied the rain as players headed for the clubhouse but ironically Goosen, who has an understandable fear of lightning, did not hear it.
"I'm glad I didn't notice the thunder or I would have been worried," Goosen said.
"I was hit by lightning 10 years ago at Petersburg as I passed by a tree, suffered burns and got knocked out. It burst my eardrum and caused me a heart murmur and I was in hospital for two months.
"I'm lucky to be here and it took a lot of fitness work to get myself strong again."
McGinley bogeyed the second, his 11th hole, just before the suspension after charging to within a stroke of the lead briefly with an eagle on 18. Chapman has played nine holes and Gates six.
Lyle, playing three events in Europe on a break from the U.S. Tour, bogeyed his eighth hole after straying into heavy rough but stayed in contention with three birdies.
